title: Audit & Internal Controls
description: Ensure financial accuracy and prevent fraud. Tests control design, audit trail tracing, and fraud risk assessment.

seo.overviewTitle: Internal Audit & COSO Internal Controls Framework
seo.overviewBody: Internal audit evaluates organizational risk management, control systems, and governance processes. Internal auditors demonstrate value by auditing control environments (COSO framework), designing Risk & Control Matrices (RCM), evaluating segregation of duties, and writing working papers.

deliverables.title: 1. COSO Internal Control Evaluation Report
deliverables.desc: Audit report evaluating Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Control Activities, Information & Communication, and Monitoring.

deliverables.title: 2. Risk & Control Matrix (RCM) Document
deliverables.desc: RCM matrix identifying financial reporting risks, key preventative/detective controls, and audit testing steps.

deliverables.title: 3. Internal Audit Working Papers & Test Log
deliverables.desc: Sampled audit working papers documenting walkthrough tests, sample selection, and control deficiency findings.

faqs.question: What are the 5 components of the COSO Internal Control Framework?
faqs.answer: Control Environment, Risk Assessment, Control Activities, Information & Communication, and Monitoring Activities.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Preventative and Detective controls?
faqs.answer: Preventative controls prevent errors or fraud before they occur (e.g. dual sign-offs). Detective controls identify errors after they occur (e.g. monthly bank reconciliations).

faqs.question: Why is Segregation of Duties critical in finance departments?
faqs.answer: Segregation of duties ensures no single individual has control over all phases of a transaction (authorization, custody, recording), preventing fraud.
